title: Company-wide policies and processes — Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendors, Travel, Templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and commonly used internal templates. It is intended for all employees, managers, and process owners.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Provide a single, authoritative reference for cross-functional processes that affect security, compliance, finance and operational continuity.
- Scope: Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors who interact with corporate systems, data stores, procurement systems, or travel programs.

Document structure (quick links):
1) Access & permissions
2) Change management
3) Data management
4) Procurement & expenses
5) Vendor management
6) Travel policies
7) Internal templates and forms
8) Governance and review cadence

1) Access & permissions
Overview:
Redwood uses role-based access control (RBAC) for cloud consoles, internal services, and third-party tools. Access requests, escalations, and periodic reviews are standardized to reduce blast radius while enabling engineers and teams to work efficiently.

Key principles:
- Least privilege: Grant the minimum permissions necessary for the task.
- Separation of duties: Approvals must come from a manager and a security owner for privileged roles.
- Time-boxed access: Temporary elevated access must include an expiration timestamp.

Request and approval process (standard):
1. Initiator opens an access request in the Access Portal (internal link) with justification, duration, and affected resources.
2. Manager reviews and approves/rejects within 48 hours.
3. Security or Service Owner performs risk review for privileged roles (e.g., infra-admin, kube-admin) and approves within 24 hours.
4. Provisioning is automated via the Identity Provider (IdP) with audit logging; request is closed when access is granted.

Emergency access (break-glass):
1. Use the emergency access flow in PagerDuty (tag: emergency-access).
2. On-call SRE or a designated approver can grant temporary access for a maximum of 4 hours.
3. An incident ticket must be opened describing the change; follow-up review within 3 business days.

Periodic review:
- Quarterly access review for all high-privilege roles.
- Biannual audit for sensitive data owners.

Service owners and responsibilities:
- People Ops: maintain group membership policies and onboarding/offboarding checklist.
- Security: maintain documented role definitions and approve privileged roles.
- Team managers: approve routine access and validate justifications.

2) Change management
Goal:
Ensure predictable, auditable, and low-risk changes to production infrastructure and critical services.

Change types and approvals:
- Standard change: pre-authorized (e.g., routine instance patching). Requires change ticket and notification, no CAB review.
- Normal change: non-emergency changes that require a scheduled change window and CAB approval for high risk.
- Emergency change: fixes to restore service. Post-facto CAB review required.

Change process (normal changes):
1. Submit a change request in the Change Management system including scope, rollback plan, and test plan.
2. Technical reviewer (service owner) reviews and assigns risk (Low/Medium/High).
3. For Medium/High risk, schedule in weekly CAB. CAB includes: engineering triage lead, SRE, security rep, and product owner.
4. Execute in the approved maintenance window; update the change record with results.
5. Post-deployment verification and close the change.

Minimum requirements for all changes:
- Impact analysis (who, what, when)
- Backout/rollback plan with steps and owner
- Pre/post validation checklist
- Communication plan (status, customer impact)

Emergency change handling:
- Emergency changes may be executed immediately with 2 approvers (on-call SRE and service owner).
- An after-action review (AAR) and CAB review must be performed within 5 business days.

Change windows and blackout periods:
- Regular maintenance windows: Sat 02:00–06:00 UTC (low traffic).
- Product launches and major events: subject to blackout periods declared by Product.

3) Data management
Data classification:
- Public: safe for public disclosure.
- Internal: company-internal information, low risk.
- Confidential: sensitive business data (contracts, pricing).
- Restricted: personal data, customer PII, financials, health data. Access requires explicit approval and encryption at rest.

Handling and storage requirements by classification (table):
| Classification | Encryption at rest | Backup frequency | Retention baseline | Access review cadence |
|---------------|--------------------|------------------|--------------------|-----------------------|
| Public        | Optional           | N/A              | 1 year             | Annual                |
| Internal      | Optional           | Daily            | 2 years            | Annual                |
| Confidential  | Required           | Daily            | 7 years            | Quarterly             |
| Restricted    | Required (KMS)     | Hourly snapshots | According to contract| Quarterly             |

Data lifecycle procedures:
- Ingestion: validate schema and classification tag at creation.
- Storage: use approved storage services only (see approved-services list).
- Sharing: use secure links with expiration and minimum privilege. No unrestricted public buckets.
- Deletion: follow retention policy; for restricted data, use verified secure-delete and update inventory.

Backups and disaster recovery:
- Daily backups for critical systems; hourly snapshots for restricted data stores.
- Recovery Time Objective (RTO): 4 hours for core APIs; Recovery Point Objective (RPO): 1 hour for critical data.
- DR runbooks maintained by SRE team; annual DR exercises required.

Data retention and legal holds:
- Retention baselines are above; legal or regulatory holds supersede retention—People Ops or Legal will notify Data Owners to suspend deletion operations.

Data breach response:
- Follow Security Incident Response runbook (link).
- Notify Legal and CISO within 2 hours of confirmed data exfiltration.

4) Procurement & expenses
Overview:
Procurement and expenses must balance velocity with financial controls. This section standardizes thresholds, approvals, and expense reimbursements.

Approval matrix (high level):
- <= $2,500: Team manager approval.
- > $2,500 and <= $25,000: Department head + Finance approval.
- > $25,000: VP-level + Finance + Legal review.
- Recurring SaaS contracts: review at $1,000/month threshold.

Procurement process (steps):
1. Create a Purchase Request in the procurement portal with justification, vendor, and budget code.
2. Manager approves; Finance verifies budget availability.
3. For contracts > $25k, Legal performs standard review and redlines.
4. PO issuance by Finance; vendor onboarding checklist executed by Procurement team.

Corporate card and expense policy:
- Corporate cards assigned on request with manager approval.
- Personal reimbursements: submit expense report within 30 days with receipts.
- Allowed expenses: travel, customer meals (per policy), reasonable software and hardware with prior approval.
- Disallowed: cash advances without approval, personal entertainment unrelated to work.

Travel & pre-approvals for procurement:
- All travel > $1,500 estimated requires manager pre-approval.

5) Vendor management
Vendor onboarding checklist:
- Business justification and PO/contract reference.
- Security questionnaire (complete vendor security assessment).
- Data flow diagram (if vendor will store/process restricted/confidential data).
- SLA negotiation and performance metrics.
- Reference and compliance checks for regulated vendors.

Vendor classification and controls:
- Low-risk: non-sensitive SaaS with no customer data. Quarterly review.
- Medium-risk: vendors with internal access or non-sensitive customer metadata. Monthly health checks.
- High-risk: vendors handling Restricted or Confidential customer data — require SOC2/ISO27001 evidence, contractual security clauses, and quarterly audits.

Contract and renewal management:
- Contract owner (procurement) tracks renewal 90/60/30 days before expiry.
- Vendors automatically re-reviewed for risk and spend at renewal.

Offboarding a vendor:
1. Termination notice sent per contract.
2. Revoke all credentials and network access.
3. Verify data return or secure deletion per contract; obtain certificate of destruction if applicable.
4. Update inventory and notify stakeholders.

6) Travel policies (summary)
Booking and approvals:
- Employees must use the company travel portal for booking approved hotels and flights.
- Domestic travel: manager approval required for trips > 1 day.
- International travel: manager + People Ops approval.

Per diem and allowable expenses:
- Meals: up to $75/day in major metros, $50/day in smaller cities; receipts required for amounts over $25.
- Lodging: book within corporate rate guidelines.
- Ground transportation: use ride-share or approved car service; receipts required.

Travel safety and international travel:
- Register all international travel in the Travel Registry.
- Security briefing for high-risk countries; employees must consult People Ops at least 14 days before travel.

Expense reimbursement process:
1. Submit expense report in the Expenses portal within 30 days of trip end.
2. Attach itemized receipts and provide business purpose.
3. Manager approves; Finance processes payment within next payroll cycle.

7) Internal templates and forms
Available templates (links to the portal):
- Access Request template (for onboarding and temporary access)
- Change Request template (includes rollback and test checklist)
- Vendor Security Questionnaire (VSA)
- Purchase Request & PO template
- Travel Authorization form
- Offboarding checklist (employees and vendors)

How to use templates:
- Fill required fields; incomplete templates will be returned for completion.
- Use the current version stored in the Templates library (version control enforced).

8) Governance, training and review cadence
Owners and cadence:
- People Ops: owner for onboarding/offboarding, travel and general policy coordination (review cadence: annual).
- Finance: owner for procurement, cards and expense policy (review cadence: annual + quarterly spend reviews).
- Security: owner for access controls and vendor security posture (review cadence: quarterly).
- SRE: owner for change management and DR (review cadence: semi-annual).

Training and awareness:
- Mandatory annual training: Security Basics, Data Handling, and Procurement & Expenses.
- Role-based training: managers and service owners must complete change management training on hire and annually.

Policy exceptions and escalation:
- Exceptions must be requested via the Policy Exception form and include compensating controls.
- Exceptions require approval from the relevant owner and Security or Finance depending on the area.
